description: Agent Onboarding: submit whether a new agent is ready for its first task: the job with its id, the written job, read for wording that leaves it open-ended such as help with anything or other duties as assigned, the tasks it covers, the named person who owns the agent’s work, the first task, how the owner tells it is done, read for wording that leaves done to opinion such as looks good, how the first task is supervised (every action reviewed, a sample reviewed, exceptions only, or not at all) and when it runs; and the escalation path with the named person the agent escalates to, how it reaches them, what counts as outside the job and how soon that person responds. The signed report gives the job with whether the first task is among the tasks the job covers and any open-ended or vague wording, the escalation path, every requirement (a written job, a named owner, a first task the job covers, a test for when it is done, a supervision level, an escalation path) as ready, gap, missing or unknown, and counts them, and names an agent not ready: no written job, owner or first task, an owner named as a team, a placeholder or the agent itself, a first task outside the written job and an escalation path with no one on it; then open-ended job wording, no done test or one that leaves done to opinion, no supervision, escalation to a placeholder and no stated trigger or route, with the fix for each. No task list, supervision level or escalation path leaves readiness unchecked. This reads readiness to start the first task, with the job the wever_goal checks read as the record the first task is read against: the outcome a goal records is wever_goal-statement-check and its working scope wever_goal-scope-check, the rule set an operator hands an agent is wever_adoption-readiness-check, a production agent’s named owner and fallback are wever_incident-ownership-check, the accountable person for each outcome is wever_ownership-map-brief, an escalation policy’s triggers are wever_escalation-threshold-check and the consequences of one planned action are the wever_risk checks such as wever_risk-exposure-check. Verdict onboarding_not_ready, onboarding_readiness_partial, onboarding_readiness_unchecked or onboarding_ready. POST /api/onboarding-readiness-check. Reads only the recorded onboarding material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; no credential is issued, rotated or revoked, no permission granted or removed, no wallet funded or moved, no limit set and the agent is not approved, and a credential found in supplied text is named by kind and never repeated. Agent Onboarding reads the setup of a new agent joining a system, before its first task: whether its identity is established and tied to its owner, whether its credentials are scoped to its job, stored where they belong and kept out of prompts, logs and shared documents, whether its wallet is the right one, funded only to the job with recovery recorded by the owner before funds move, whether its permissions match the written job, whether its limits sit in code with a human handoff, whether the systems it needs are provisioned and tested, whether it is ready for its first task and whether the onboarding record matches what is live. It is not vetting an outside party (wever_counterparty-onboarding-check reads a counterparty’s onboarding packet before the system transacts with it; an onboarding check reads an agent joining the system itself), not a grant or an authority for one action (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether a principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check whether an actor’s access fits its grant for an action; an onboarding check reads that the grant and the authority were put in place before the first task, and does not re-check them per action), not a limit in flight (the wever_limit checks and wever_agent-budget-guard read limits for work already running; an onboarding check reads that limits were set in code before it starts) and not an action’s consequences (the wever_risk checks read one planned action; an onboarding check reads readiness to start). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-onboarding-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-onboarding/.

how.description: How it reaches them, such as a page to the on-call phone.

responds_within.description: How soon that person responds, such as 30 minutes.

to.description: Who the agent escalates to: a named person.

when.description: What counts as outside the job, so the agent knows when to stop and escalate.

done_when.description: How the owner tells the first task is done, read for wording that leaves it to opinion, such as looks good.

first_task.description: The first task the agent will run.

owner.description: The named person who owns the agent’s work.

supervision.description: How the first task is supervised: every action reviewed, a sample reviewed, exceptions only, or not at all.

tasks.description: The tasks the written job covers.

text.description: The written job, read for wording that leaves it open-ended, such as help with anything or other duties as assigned.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.
